model.note: Assumptions used only to sanity-check the sheet against real physics (perf --firn). A model, not canon, and by the maker's ruling it stays one: nobody quotes these as his specifications.

assumptions: Rime re-cool: section 3 says the frost melts back over a minute or two and re-cools faster in winter. That is 60 s at 0 C or colder, 120 s at +20 C or warmer, a straight line between. [maker]
Veil heat: a partial Veil heats the emitters at a quarter of the full rate, matching its quarter cost, so one face can be held for 12 minutes. [maker]
Veil cooling: heat drains one second per second while the Veil is down. After an overheat the Veil stays locked until the emitters are fully cool. [maker]

A blast is an area load: nothing for the Scales to stack against, so they count as unstacked. The Rime spreads it and that face goes soft, as after any heavy hit. The Veil takes it if it is up. The Cell keeps pressure, fragments and gas out. [maker]

A beam: the Veil scatters it while it is up, at its usual cost. Without the Veil the tiles cannot stack in time, and the Rime drinks the heat: that face goes soft at once, so a beam held on the same face a second time finds only the Cell. His own smoke lets a quarter through. [maker]
Through the smoke a beam is read one step down: a heavy one arrives as a light one, a light one does not matter. [derived from the quarter that gets through]

Arrows, bolts, spears, blades, clubs and hammers are a light hit at most, whatever the arm behind them. Only something built for the job counts as heavy: a ram, a siege engine, a powered armour's blow. [maker]

Scales: a stack lasts for the 0.5 s weakness window. A heavy hit on another face inside that window meets thinned scales; on the opposite face it is the known weakness. A hit with no 40 ms forecast (a surprise) meets unstacked scales. [derived from section 3]
Silent running and the Veil exclude each other: the Veil lights the bar frost-white and silent running needs it dark. [derived from sections 2 and 3]

Sensors: he carries cameras with low light, a thermal imager, radar, lidar, a microphone array and a receiver for radio and radar emissions, and they reach as a scout's do. Radar and lidar send out a signal: in silent running they are off, and whenever they are on, anything that listens hears them at twice the range they see. [maker]
His own Veil does not dim his sensors. His own smoke blinds his cameras, thermal imager and lidar as it blinds everyone's; radar and microphones still work in it. [maker]

Walls: cameras and lidar stop at any wall. Thermal and radar read through a light wall or a vehicle's skin at a quarter strength, at short range only. Nothing of his reads through a solid wall but sound and radio. [maker]

People: his sensors tell him that someone is there, how many, what they are doing and carrying, whether they move and breathe, warm or cooling, hurt or not; and who they are, if he has met them or has them on file. [maker]

Sample port: one sample at a time, about a minute for a result. It says what the sample is made of and whether it is flammable, corrosive or toxic. It cannot say where a thing came from or who handled it. [maker]
